title: Unfair dismissal

draft.title: Unfair dismissal
card: Dismissal is when an employer ends a worker's job. An employer can lawfully dismiss a worker, but the dismissal must not be harsh, unjust or unreasonable.
A worker who thinks they were dismissed unfairly can apply to the Fair Work Commission. The Commission is the national workplace tribunal under the Fair Work Act 2009.
The Commission looks at whether there was a valid reason, such as poor conduct or performance. It also looks at whether the worker was told the reason and given a chance to respond.
If the claim succeeds, the Commission can order reinstatement, which returns the worker to their job. It can order compensation, which is money paid to the worker, if reinstatement is not suitable.
draft.remember: An unfair sacking can be challenged at the Fair Work Commission, which may order reinstatement or compensation.

a.q: Which action is open to a worker who believes they were sacked in a harsh, unjust or unreasonable way?
opts: Apply to the Fair Work Commission for a remedy
Apply to SafeWork NSW for a safety order
Ask the employer's customers to hold a vote
Sign a new enterprise agreement with the employer
a.why: The Fair Work Commission hears unfair dismissal claims and can order a remedy. SafeWork NSW is tempting, but it deals with workplace safety and not with dismissals.
a.clue: Which body hears claims about sackings?

b.q: Dev is sacked from a bakery in Orange after a customer complaint. His manager never told him about the complaint and gave him no chance to respond. Dev applies to the Fair Work Commission. Which factor most supports his claim that the dismissal was unfair?
opts: He was not given a chance to respond to the reason
He was sacked for a reason his employer disliked
He had worked at the bakery for many years
He was paid the same wage as other bakers
b.why: The Commission considers whether the worker was given a chance to respond to the reason for dismissal. Being sacked after a complaint does not make a dismissal unfair, because a dismissal can be lawful if it follows a fair process and a valid reason.
b.clue: Think about the process the employer followed, not only the reason.

a.best: Apply to the Fair Work Commission for a remedy

b.best: He was not given a chance to respond to the reason

check.summary: No problems found. The card matches the Fair Work Act unfair dismissal provisions: valid reason, notice and a chance to respond, and reinstatement as the main remedy with compensation when reinstatement is not suitable. Both questions have one clearly right answer.
